I'll think through this as the farmer.

---

Alright, let me sit down and plan out this year. I have 5 mu total, and I've been doing this for 20 years so I know my land.

My main rotation is wheat-maize — winter wheat then summer maize on the same ground. That's what everyone around here does, and it works. But I also keep a little cotton and a little peanut on separate patches because they bring in cash and peanut is good for the soil. So this is how I split it:

- **5 mu winter wheat** (October to June) — all my land goes to wheat in winter
- **3 mu summer maize** (June to October) — main summer crop
- **1 mu cotton** — on the sandier corner, for cash
- **1 mu peanut** — good for the soil, and my family eats some

**Wheat:** Last year I used about one bag of compound fertilizer (40 kg) plus two bags of urea (about 100 kg) across my plot before sowing and at green-up. That comes out to around 14 kg N per mu. I'll do the same — my neighbor tried cutting back and his yield dropped. I'd rather spend the extra 50 yuan than lose 50 kg of wheat. I use improved variety (Jimai or Shixin type) that the dealer in town sells. I irrigate 3 times — before winter, at jointing, and at grain filling. I expect around 500 kg per mu if the weather holds.

**Maize:** Summer maize after wheat, straw returned to field with rotary tiller. I use Zhengdan or Xianyu hybrid seed — everyone uses hybrid now, traditional seed gives half the yield. About 16 kg N per mu, split between base and big-trumpet stage. Two irrigations usually, sometimes one if rain comes. Expect 550-600 kg per mu.

**Cotton:** Only 1 mu, on the sandy patch. I use Bt cotton seed from the dealer — don't need to spray bollworm so much. Cotton needs a lot of fertilizer but I can't spend too much on just 1 mu. About 13 kg N, heavier on potash because cotton likes it. I spray 4-5 times for aphids and spider mites.

**Peanut:** Peanut doesn't need much nitrogen — it makes its own from the roots. But it wants phosphorus and calcium. I use improved large-seed variety. Irrigate twice if dry. Expect 280 kg per mu.

Money is tight with 5 people at home, but two of us work off-farm so we can afford proper inputs. I won't cut corners on seed or fertilizer — that's how you lose the harvest.
